text:
Condition: Atopic Dermatitis
Section: Treatment
Subsection: Topical Therapies

First-Line Treatments:
- Emollients and moisturizers: Apply liberally and frequently, especially after bathing. Ointments and creams are more effective than lotions.
- Topical corticosteroids: Reduce inflammation and itching. Strength varies by location and severity.
- Topical calcineurin inhibitors: Non-steroidal option for face and skin folds.

Emollient Guidance: Regular use of emollients is fundamental to management. Apply within 3 minutes of bathing to lock in moisture. Choose fragrance-free products to minimize irritation.

Steroid Potency: Low-potency steroids for face/neck; medium-potency for trunk/extremities; high-potency for severe disease or thick-skinned areas. Rotate formulations to minimize tolerance.

Adjunctive Therapies: Phototherapy (UVB or PUVA) for moderate-to-severe disease. Systemic medications (JAK inhibitors, biologic agents) for severe, refractory cases.

Source: American Academy of Dermatology (AAD)
Source URL: https://www.aad.org/public/diseases/eczema/treatment
